newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens further on ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens further on ample supply.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in late trading on Thursday, dealers said.
"Liquidity is the main issue," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Dealers said operators were initially a bit worried about liquidity conditions on Friday due to weekly tax payments.
"But operators seem to have the confidence to accumulate some dollars in the wake of excess rupiah because tom/next swaps are falling," the U.S. bank dealer said.
Tom/next swaps fell to 0.10/0.15 from 0.8/1.0. Overnight swaps closed at -0.05/par points.
Dealers said dollar interest rates were higher than the rupiah at present. Overnight dollar was at 5.625/5.75 percent.
Overnight rupiah was last traded at 4.00/4.25 percent.
"If liquidity remains ample on Friday, we expect the dollar to strengthen further against the rupiah," one said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,394.75/95.00 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,392.75/93.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,394.50/95.00 and 2,393.0/93.5, respectively.
Dealers said short-term swaps had eased on ample rupiah but longer-term swaps were relatively stable.
One-month swaps were at 10.75/11.5, two at 23.5/25.0, three at 36.25/37.25 and six at 75.5/76.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,385/2,577 and the conversion band to 2,385/2,433 on Thursday, the third this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by three points the previous week.
